🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off Saturday: Bitcoin lost its 50-day average as ETF outflows and a tech sell-off weighed, while an Initia exploit, tokenization pushback and Netanyahu's sanctions-dodging blockchain talk kept security and policy in focus. 📉 Bitcoin Slips Below Its 50-Day Average as ETF Outflows Pile Up Bitcoin closed Friday below its 50-day moving average for the first time since mid-August, ending a 66-day streak, and drifted toward $80,500 on Saturday. US spot BTC ETFs shed about $636 million on Thursday and another $138 million on Friday, as an AI-driven tech sell-off kept risk appetite weak ahead of the Fed's October 28 decision. Read full story 🚨 Initia Halts Its Blockchain After $2.7M Infinite-Mint Exploit Initia froze its Layer 1 and connected rollups at 15:41 UTC on Friday after an attacker abused a flaw in a Move minting function to create unbacked AUSD tokens. Roughly $2.7 million in assets was moved out to Ethereum before the halt; the team has not yet confirmed total losses or a restart timeline. More details 🏛️ SEC Puts "Super Intelligence" and Tokenization on Its 2027 Exam Radar The SEC's Division of Examinations published its fiscal 2027 priorities, replacing "artificial intelligence" with "super intelligence and other advanced technologies" and naming tokenization as a key risk area. Crypto oversight now sits almost entirely under the tokenization heading, signalling where examiners will focus as on-chain stock trading expands. Read more 🏦 Wells Fargo, Arm and Intuit Block Tokenization of Their Shares Six more companies, including Wells Fargo, Arm Holdings and Intuit, have refused to let OKXICE, the OKX and Intercontinental Exchange joint venture, offer tokenized versions of their stock, Reuters reported citing a regulatory document. That brings objecting issuers to 22, against the 63 stocks the venue had planned to tokenize. See details 🇮🇱 Netanyahu Orders a Blockchain Plan to Sidestep Possible Banking Sanctions In a Friday TV interview days before Israel's election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he has asked officials to prepare a blockchain-based plan in case Israeli banks face international sanctions. He named no network, currency or timeline, and opposition leaders quickly attacked the idea as a sign of deepening economic isolation. Caption: 


----------

**Welcome back!** It's recap day, with this week's five biggest stories and five tools to try this weekend. Claude learned to work while you're away, and AI dug up decade-old holes in the code behind most websites. Banks found AI agents inside customer accounts. DeepSeek kept introducing itself as ChatGPT, and Claude cracked a 26-year-old NSA mystery in half an hour.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **Claude:** What can Claude get done while you're away?

* **PHP:** How did AI find decade-old holes in the code behind most websites?

* **Banks:** Can your bank tell if your AI agent went rogue?

* **DeepSeek:** Why does DeepSeek keep saying it's ChatGPT?

* **NSA:** How did Claude crack a 26-year-old NSA mystery in half an hour?


----------







----------
## Claude now works even when you're not using it

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/79ab6baa-eb02-42e2-8e53-8f68f568df3a/72ba3c39-79c6-482f-b365-56c0284e5072.jpg?t=1792657790)
Caption: 

Anthropic launched [Claude Duet](https://claude.com/resources/articles/claude-duet), an assistant that works in the background and keeps you updated without waiting for you to start a chat.

It runs on its own cloud computer and asks before doing anything sensitive. For now, it's a waitlist research preview for Pro and Max subscribers in the US.

Then Anthropic said [sessions in Claude's apps](https://x.com/claudeai/status/2113360845409583307) will run in auto mode by default starting next week, so Claude stops asking you to approve every step.

Claude is getting comfortable working without you.


----------







----------
## AI found decade-old holes in the code behind most websites

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/778c44dd-6634-4f03-acb5-507e4041f55a/b20c7654-9b8a-426f-89c8-0418a3adc82f.jpg?t=1792657786)
Caption: 

Two critical flaws had been hiding for more than a decade in PHP, the code behind about 70% of websites. [Wiz found them](https://www.wiz.io/blog/php2shell-php-rce) with help from AI models made by OpenAI and Google.

Cloudflare saw thousands of attack attempts before the bugs were even announced, then millions after. The NSA told companies to patch or go offline.

By the end of the week, people online were calling it [Black October](https://tech.yahoo.com/cybersecurity/articles/black-october-disclosure-wave-label-023233848.html) as one hack
